name: FakeCompanyABC Retrieval Ground Truth - 100 Question Hard Benchmark

design.purpose: A larger and deliberately harder retrieval benchmark created before adding reranking, with paraphrases, thresholds, temporal confusion, negative conditions, scenarios, cross-policy questions, and multi-evidence questions.
design.relevance_definition: Evidence relevance remains exact source evidence. relevant_sources is additionally provided for coarse source-level evaluation and may include referenced policies that are legitimately useful even when the exact answer sentence is in another file.
design.verification: Every evidence exact_text string was programmatically verified as a verbatim substring of its named source Markdown file.
design.evaluation_note: Freeze retrieval settings before using this benchmark for comparison. Do not tune thresholds on these same 100 questions and then report the tuned score as an unbiased test result.

questions.question: A full-time employee is German but their employment contract is based in Pakistan. How much annual leave does the company policy give them each year?
questions.expected_answer: 24 working days, because entitlement follows contractual work location rather than nationality.

evidence.exact_text: Full-time employees whose contractual work location is Pakistan receive **24 working days of paid annual leave per calendar year**.
The annual entitlement is based on the employee's **contractual work location**, not nationality, citizenship, or the country from which the employee happens to work temporarily.

questions.question: A Germany-contracted employee spends several months temporarily working from Pakistan. Without a contract change, which annual-leave entitlement continues to apply?
questions.expected_answer: The Germany entitlement continues to apply: 30 working days per calendar year.

evidence.exact_text: - A Germany-based employee temporarily working from Pakistan still follows the Germany annual-leave entitlement unless the employment contract is changed.
Full-time employees whose contractual work location is Germany receive **30 working days of paid annual leave per calendar year**.

questions.question: An employee finishes the year with 8 unused leave days. What is the maximum number the policy lets them take into the next year?
questions.expected_answer: 5 days.

evidence.exact_text: Employees may carry forward a maximum of **5 unused annual-leave days** into the following calendar year.
- An employee contracted in Germany with 8 unused days at year-end may carry forward only 5 days.

questions.question: If carried-over leave is still unused on 1 April, what normally happens, and what can prevent that outcome?
questions.expected_answer: It normally expires after 31 March unless HR approved an exception in writing.

evidence.exact_text: Carried-forward leave must normally be used by **31 March** of the following year. Any remaining carried-forward leave expires after that date unless HR has approved an exception in writing.

questions.question: Someone wants six consecutive working days off. What notice period should they normally allow?
questions.expected_answer: At least 3 weeks in advance.

evidence.exact_text: Leave of **more than 5 consecutive working days** should normally be requested at least **3 weeks in advance**.

questions.question: Someone wants exactly five consecutive working days off. What notice period normally applies?
questions.expected_answer: At least 5 working days in advance.

evidence.exact_text: Leave of **5 consecutive working days or fewer** should normally be requested at least **5 working days in advance**.

questions.question: How does the normal advance-notice rule change when a leave request goes from exactly 5 consecutive working days to 6?
questions.expected_answer: Exactly 5 days normally needs 5 working days of notice; more than 5 days normally needs at least 3 weeks.

evidence.exact_text: Leave of **5 consecutive working days or fewer** should normally be requested at least **5 working days in advance**.
Leave of **more than 5 consecutive working days** should normally be requested at least **3 weeks in advance**.

questions.question: Does giving sufficient advance notice remove the need for manager approval for annual leave?
questions.expected_answer: No. All annual-leave requests still require approval from the direct manager.

evidence.exact_text: All annual-leave requests require approval from the employee's direct manager.

questions.question: Does being on probation reduce a full-time employee’s annual-leave entitlement?
questions.expected_answer: No. The entitlement itself is not reduced during probation, although requests still depend on business needs and manager approval.
